source.note: Refreshed 2026-10-03. Relative to the previously pinned Hebrew blob 954f82559e618a091bb338c65a61be9e50d48331, the only semantic-surface delta is a non-semantic Hebrew wording cleanup in the Seer beta sentence: 'production קבוע' -> 'שירות קבוע בסביבת ייצור'. The claim register remains semantically valid.

authority.rule: Every claim below describes what the current public explanation says. It is not promoted to canon by appearing in this register.

claims.summary: The displayed Pastafarian date is a function F(c,t) of calculation/working day c and target day t, not of t alone.
claims.futureAction: Reconcile directly against corpus definition of date mapping.

claims.summary: The same target day may receive a different Pastafarian date under a different working day.
claims.futureAction: Reconcile directly against corpus and preserve explanatory example only if true.

claims.summary: The calendar is described as the calendar in which time was created.
claims.futureAction: Check exact corpus ontology/origin wording; this is high-risk public framing.

claims.summary: A Pastafarian date has exactly five fields: year, cutlet name, day in cutlet, month name, day in month.
claims.futureAction: Reconcile field count/order/semantics directly against corpus.

claims.summary: Working day, observer location, chronological identity and technical metadata may accompany the date but are not a sixth date field.
claims.futureAction: Check corpus/data-model distinction; retain as explanatory product guidance if compatible.

claims.summary: Changing c can change years, cutlets, months, names and weaving, not merely relabel a fixed structure.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: An almanac computed today need not remain useful tomorrow.
claims.futureAction: Keep only if the corpus semantics still support the premise; wording is editorial.

claims.summary: A stable chronological day identity/day-id is distinguished from its Pastafarian representation.
claims.futureAction: Check product/domain-model contract; corpus governs semantics, not necessarily identifier naming.

claims.summary: Meetings, births and historical events should remain anchored to a stable chronological identity while their Pastafarian presentation may change.
claims.futureAction: Retain as product guidance if consistent with corpus.

claims.summary: If c=t, the year is always 5000.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Year 5000 does not imply c=t.
claims.futureAction: Determine whether corpus states this or it remains derived; revalidate if underlying rules change.

claims.summary: Y>5000 implies t>c and Y<5000 implies t<c.
claims.futureAction: Reprove/revalidate against corpus implementation.

claims.summary: Year 0 exists and negative-numbered years exist farther into the past.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Year length is between 252 and 5778 days.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Year boundaries and cutlet boundaries are built from the gate system.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Years need not align to seasons, solar orbit or lunar cycle.
claims.futureAction: Retain if implied by corpus; not itself an extra rule.

claims.summary: Each year has 6–17 cutlets.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: A cutlet is a contiguous chronological segment.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Cutlet length is at least 42 days.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: There are 17 canonical cutlet names and no within-year repeated name.
claims.futureAction: Reconcile semantic naming identity and repetition rules against corpus.

claims.summary: Each year has 3–47 structural months.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Each month has 4–123 member days.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: A month need not be chronologically contiguous; its day number is ordinal occurrence within that month.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Months can interleave; each chronological day belongs to exactly one month.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: There are constraints on first/last occurrence ordering even though months need not finish before another starts.
claims.futureAction: Reconcile exact constraint formulation with corpus.

claims.summary: Cutlets and months are distinct coordinate systems over the same days.
claims.futureAction: Retain as explanatory consequence if corpus supports premises.

claims.summary: Day n+1 of a month is the next occurrence of that month and need not be the next chronological day.
claims.futureAction: Revalidate from month semantics; explanatory wording only.

claims.summary: Being near the final ordinal day of a month does not imply chronological proximity to that occurrence.
claims.futureAction: Retain if interleaving semantics remain.

claims.summary: The current specification defines no canonical week system, week-day names or same-weekday relation.
claims.futureAction: Ask corpus explicitly whether absence remains canonical; absence claims are sensitive to added canon.

claims.summary: An external civil week system may be overlaid without becoming part of the Pastafarian date.
claims.futureAction: Retain if compatible with corpus/product scope.

claims.summary: There are 17 cutlet names and 47 month names.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Name identity is semantic/canonical rather than a vote among spellings, translations or implementations.
claims.futureAction: Directly align with corpus naming model.

claims.summary: The current article says the Hebrew Scroll is the supreme authority for name meaning.
claims.futureAction: P0 authority migration: replace/refine according to new corpus hierarchy.

claims.summary: Translation/transliteration are presentation layers rather than semantic identity.
claims.futureAction: Reconcile with corpus naming/localization rules and propagate to Seer/app locale policy.

claims.summary: 47 names × 123 ordinal days gives 5781 syntactic month/day pairs.
claims.futureAction: Recompute if name count or max month length changes.

claims.summary: With year length ≤5778, at least three possible month/day pairs are absent in every year.
claims.futureAction: Reprove mechanically from corpus bounds; do not treat as independent canon.

claims.summary: Q=2^127−1 is central to the calculation.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus algorithm reconciliation.

claims.summary: The current article lists five input counts, 7 hidden drops, 46 visible drops, 6 bowls and 12 final stirs.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus algorithm reconciliation.

claims.summary: Each final stir computes all six new bowls from one old snapshot before simultaneous commit.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus algorithm reconciliation.

claims.summary: R=SAVE(S+149r), not raw S, is used both for permutation and additive term inside final-stir update.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation; if changed, invalidate dependent vectors/research.

claims.summary: Older raw-sum-derived examples are described as obsolete unless reverified.
claims.futureAction: Preserve historical status if corpus confirms; otherwise annotate, do not rewrite history.

claims.summary: Short Choice uses rejection sampling to avoid simple modulo bias.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Wide Choice is not equivalent to independent uniform base-Q digits until an index is formed.
claims.futureAction: Reconcile exact algorithm and preserve negative warning only if still true.

claims.summary: For sufficiently large spaces, legal options may be unreachable under the specific Wide Choice mechanism.
claims.futureAction: Reprove against corpus algorithm.

claims.summary: Structural Atlas values are empirical observations from a computation corpus, not canonical rules.
claims.futureAction: Preserve classification; rerun only if premises/engine version change.

claims.summary: Article records a specific engine identifier, sample sizes and many observed statistics.
claims.futureAction: Do not copy into canon; validate provenance and optionally regenerate after corpus alignment.

claims.summary: Recurrence may be defined by month/day, cutlet/day or combined conditions.
claims.futureAction: Check corpus field semantics; final recurrence policy is product/editorial.

claims.summary: A Pastafarian yearly recurrence is a search problem rather than simple RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY.
claims.futureAction: Retain if semantics still make recurrence nontrivial.

claims.summary: Article reports exact scan horizons and recurrence-distribution statistics.
claims.futureAction: Revalidate only if underlying semantics or scan implementation change.

claims.summary: Scheduling by Pastafarian date requires agreement on the five-field date and the working day used.
claims.futureAction: Check against corpus representation uniqueness and product contract.

claims.summary: Important appointments may additionally store an absolute chronological day/instant.
claims.futureAction: Likely product best practice; not canon.

claims.summary: An event remains fixed while its local Pastafarian label may change with location.
claims.futureAction: Check day-boundary/location semantics and product model.

claims.summary: A Pastafarian all-day event spans local Pastafarian day boundary to the next, not civil midnight to midnight.
claims.futureAction: Reconcile boundary definition with corpus; retain export warning if true.

claims.summary: The local day boundary is the topocentric lower culmination of Venus's center on the local meridian.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation; clarify whether astronomy definition is canon or product interpretation.

claims.summary: Boundary is not civil midnight, not defined by timezone/DST, and does not require naked-eye visibility.
claims.futureAction: Retain only as consequence of exact corpus definition.

claims.summary: The same instant can fall in different Pastafarian local days at different locations.
claims.futureAction: Revalidate from boundary definition.

claims.summary: When no usable user location exists, the product defaults to Kisurra.
claims.futureAction: Recheck live product behavior; not canon.

claims.summary: A printed calendar is valid for its stated working day and may need replacement when c changes.
claims.futureAction: Retain if F(c,t) semantics remain.

claims.summary: The current specification is described as deterministic and complete enough to calculate by hand.
claims.futureAction: High sensitivity: corpus must substantiate completeness/determinism before retaining.

claims.summary: Seer is not the source of authority and is wrong if it disagrees with the correct normative result.
claims.futureAction: Preserve non-authority architecture unless corpus explicitly changes it; update authority referent from Scroll/canonical implementation to corpus hierarchy.

claims.summary: Current article says the Scroll sets the rules and canonical calculation produces the date.
claims.futureAction: P0 migration to new corpus authority model.

claims.summary: Article records a dated list of Seer APIs/clients/native/container capabilities.
claims.futureAction: Reverify live product state; corpus does not decide capabilities.

claims.summary: Article describes live HTTPS beta deployment testing on Render.
claims.futureAction: Reverify current deployment/status; keep date if historical evidence rather than current claim.

claims.summary: Computational anchors are distinguished from origin/history of delivery.
claims.futureAction: Retain distinction if corpus uses same separation.

claims.summary: Foundation Day is stated as 22 Dec 41,222 BCE proleptic Gregorian.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus anchor reconciliation.

claims.summary: Foundation Day is explicitly not the beginning of time; it is a computational anchor.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Days around Foundation use positive odd/even encoding on opposite sides.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Tablets Day is stated as 15 Jun 763 BCE Julian / 7 Jun 763 BCE Gregorian.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation.

claims.summary: Exact distance Foundation→Tablets is stated as 14,777,149 days.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus reconciliation and arithmetic verification.

claims.summary: The calendar is described as part of creation.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus origin reconciliation.

claims.summary: Humanity is said to have used it without sufficient awareness until modern re-delivery.
claims.futureAction: Direct corpus provenance/history reconciliation.

claims.summary: The Scroll is said not to specify every historical detail; unstated details are not part of its text.
claims.futureAction: Replace/refine within corpus provenance model.

claims.summary: Modern re-delivery is a fixed historical event but has no single fixed Pastafarian date; representation depends on working day.
claims.futureAction: Corpus must settle event description/date; dynamic representation follows F(c,t) if retained.

claims.summary: Within a known year and working day, cutlet-name/day or month-name/day identify at most one day; full date is unique.
claims.futureAction: Reprove against corpus rules and implementation.

claims.summary: Article provides candidate-count upper bounds for partial known fields.
claims.futureAction: Recompute if structural bounds change.

claims.summary: A full Pastafarian five-field date without working day is not an absolute chronological address.
claims.futureAction: Reprove/revalidate; likely central explanatory result.

claims.summary: For fixed c, sufficiently far in the past there is exact affine periodicity preserving four non-year fields with a fixed year shift.
claims.futureAction: Reprove against aligned semantics; do not make canon.

claims.summary: The fixed-c theorem does not imply F(c+T,t+T)=F(c,t).
claims.futureAction: Retain as logical warning if theorem remains.

claims.summary: Whether final asymptotic slope varies among working days remains open.
claims.futureAction: Preserve as open unless later research closes it.

claims.summary: Invertibility/history-retention results are explicitly derived research, not additional calendar rules.
claims.futureAction: Preserve classification.

claims.summary: Visible stages 3–46 are described as generically injective on the relevant asymptotic branch.
claims.futureAction: Reprove if algorithm changes.

claims.summary: First five final post-stirs are said to be generically invertible on the relevant canonical union without side information.
claims.futureAction: Reprove if algorithm changes.

claims.summary: Whether final six bowls alone are always generically sufficient remains open.
claims.futureAction: Preserve as open unless research updates.

claims.summary: Summary restates core semantics and product consequences.
claims.futureAction: Rewrite last from reconciled sections; never use summary as independent authority.
